direction_as_read: positive on breath hydrogen and symptoms in single-dose lactose challenges, with one of two pre-specified primary comparisons not reaching significance; infant colic evidence inconclusive
summary: Six labels print lactase with no amount and five print 50 or 690 mg; none shown here prints FCC or ALU activity, which is how the trials dose it. 36149331 is the only trial read with a named primary outcome: 4662 FCC lactase beat placebo in one crossover (P < 0.001) and not in the other (P = 0.102). 33490624 and the stored 20391953 are positive with no named primary or amount. All are single challenges, not ongoing use. One label prints an infant purpose; the colic systematic review (38426798) calls the evidence inconclusive.
question_for_clinician: Lactase has a plausible, repeatedly positive short-term effect, but trials dose by FCC or similar activity and labels print mg or nothing. Can credit be given without a printed activity? Agent recommendation: no credit for these labels as printed; if credit is considered, tie it to a printed activity near the studied 4662 FCC, and limit it to lactose intolerance in adults.
